mainEntity.name: Is the OM654 engine in the GLA 200 d and 220 d reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM654 is a highly refined and efficient engine, praised for its lightweight all-aluminium construction and reduced friction losses. However, it has several well-documented issues that owners should be aware of. EGR cooler thermal cracking causing coolant loss. AdBlue system crystallisation on urban-driven vehicles. Timing chain and injector issues on higher-mileage units. With regular maintenance and long journeys, 150,000+ miles is realistic.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of OM654 EGR cooler failure in a GLA diesel?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM654's EGR cooler typically fails between 40,000-70,000 miles, with several warning signs. Coolant level dropping with no visible external leak. White smoke from the exhaust. Check engine light illuminated. Decrease in engine performance and rough idle. Increased fuel consumption.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my GLA 200 d or 220 d engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., EGR cooler, AdBlue dosing module, injectors). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic timing chain failure. EGR cooler replacement at specialist: £600-£950 - excellent value if caught early. AdBlue dosing module replacement: £500-£800 - sensible repair for urban-driven cars. Full OM654 rebuild: £2,800-£5,500 - for catastrophic failure or 100k+ miles. Given GLA 200 d / 220 d values (£18,000-£35,000), a rebuilt engine is typically good value.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz GLA Class 200 d / 220 d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Benz GLA 200 d and 220 d rely on the OM654 2.0-litre modular diesel - a lightweight, all-aluminium engine praised for refinement and efficiency, but not without its vulnerabilities. EGR cooler thermal cracking, AdBlue system failures, and turbocharger issues dominate replacement demand, particularly on post-2020 H247 models. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common GLA 200 d and 220 d engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: OM654 EGR Cooler Thermal Cracking - Why the GLA 200 d / 220 d Loses Coolant
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz GLA Class GLA 200 d, GLA 220 d (OM654.920, 2020-present)
problems.rootCause: The OM654's exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) cooler is subject to thermal cycling between exhaust gas temperatures and coolant. Differential expansion causes microscopic cracks in the cooler matrix, allowing coolant to be drawn into the intake manifold. The result is progressive coolant loss, white exhaust smoke, and eventually hydrolock if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace EGR cooler with updated design, flush cooling system, reset adaptions
repairOptions.longevity: 40k-70k miles. Viable if caught early with no secondary damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: EGR cooler replacement plus intake manifold cleaning to remove coolant residue and carbon
repairOptions.longevity: 40k-70k miles. Required if coolant has fouled intake valves

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt OM654 engine with updated EGR cooler, intake manifold, and emissions system components
repairOptions.longevity: 80,000+ mile lifespan. Necessary when coolant ingestion has bent a conrod or caused cylinder bore scoring

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical H247 GLA 200 d or 220 d is worth £18,000-£35,000 depending on age, mileage and condition - the full replacement cost of £2,800-£5,500 is modest relative to vehicle value, making a specialist rebuilt engine a sound investment. For vehicles worth under £15,000, evaluate repair options first.
problems.recommendation: On a newer GLA 200 d or 220 d, the EGR cooler replacement at a specialist (£600-£950) is a no-brainer. However, if your car has already overheated or shown misfire symptoms, pay for a borescope inspection before committing to repairs - bent rods are not always immediately obvious. Rebuilt OM654 units with upgraded EGR systems are increasingly common as these cars age out of manufacturer warranty.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for OM654 EGR cooler repair and rebuilt engine options for your GLA 200 d / 220 d

problems.h4: OM654 AdBlue System Crystallisation - Why the GLA Diesel Won't Start or Triggers Warning Lights
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz GLA Class GLA 200 d, GLA 220 d (OM654.920, 2020-present)
problems.rootCause: The AdBlue/SCR system can crystallise in the dosing module if the vehicle is used predominantly for short journeys. Crystallisation blocks the injector, preventing AdBlue delivery and triggering countdown warnings that can prevent the car from starting.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Flush AdBlue lines, clean dosing module, reset system, software update
repairOptions.longevity: 30k-60k miles. Viable if caught early with no component failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace AdBlue dosing module, flush system, software update
repairOptions.longevity: 50k-70k miles. Required if crystallisation has damaged the module

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt OM654 engine with AdBlue system reset and emissions component inspection
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Required for catastrophic emissions system failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a GLA 200 d or 220 d worth £18,000-£35,000, the AdBlue dosing module replacement at £500-£800 is a sensible repair. The full engine replacement cost is only justified if there is additional damage.
problems.recommendation: If your GLA 200 d or 220 d throws an AdBlue warning, address it immediately - continued driving can lead to countdown mode and vehicle immobilisation. A specialist £200-£400 flush and reset is often all that's needed if caught early. However, if the dosing module has crystallised badly, replacement at £500-£800 is the right call. Ignoring AdBlue warnings can lead to significantly more expensive repairs.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for OM654 AdBlue system repair and rebuilt engine options for your GLA 200 d / 220 d

problems.h4: OM654 Timing Chain & Injector Issues - Long-Term Reliability Concerns
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz GLA Class GLA 200 d, GLA 220 d (OM654.920, 2020-present)
problems.rootCause: While the OM654 is generally robust, owners have reported injector and timing chain issues over time. The timing chain is located at the rear of the engine - a complex and costly repair when chain stretch or tensioner failure occurs. Piezo injectors can also suffer from carbon buildup, affecting spray patterns and cold starting.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Ultrasonic injector cleaning, carbon removal from injector bores, new sealing washers
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-100k miles. Viable for minor injector issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace failed piezo injectors, code to ECU, decarbonise affected cylinders
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-120k miles. Required when cleaning no longer resolves issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: 100k+ miles. Required if rattling noise or timing fault codes present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt OM654 engine with new timing chain, injectors, upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Necessary for catastrophic failure or 120k+ miles

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a GLA 200 d or 220 d worth £18,000-£35,000, timing chain replacement at £1,500-£2,500 is a justifiable investment. Full engine replacement is only justified for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: The OM654's timing chain is generally more durable than the OM651 it replaced, but rear-chain access makes replacement labour-intensive. At the first sign of rattling on cold start, have the chain inspected immediately - ignoring it can lead to catastrophic engine failure. For injector issues, start with professional cleaning before committing to replacement; OM654 piezo injectors are expensive (£300-£500 each), so replacing all four at once on a car over 100,000 miles pushes costs towards £1,200-£2,000.
